construction: 171 parts in 17 steps. Steps 1–11: 6×6 base plates with white bricks; step 6 adds tan log bricks and round bricks between them. Step 12: black 2×2 groove tiles with seventeen 1×2 round-end plates with two open studs; the open-stud pairs are the portholes. Steps 13–14: 17 child units, each carrying two ring parts (`28974a`, an embedded part). Step 17: curved-top bricks and dark-red tiles on the lower edge.
interfaces: In the wall's frame 147 parts face up and 24 face +X. The 24 belong to the 17 child units (11 × `2.7.3.1`, 6 × `1.3.2.4`), turned 90° inside the wall; through the wall's rotation they face up in the ship. The parent matrix is `0 1 0 / −1 0 0 / 0 0 1`, studs −X (port side). Its mirror is `3.16.1`.
lesson: Portholes come from open studs on a wall built flat; children inside a sideways wall are counter-rotated so they end up upright.
parent_context: The black port hull wall of the midship box (`10294 - Titanic - 3.0 Funnel & Main Cabins.ldr`).
reuse_notes: Use open-stud plates on a flat-built wall for portholes; counter-rotate any child that must end up upright.
